title: Sienna Spiro’s ‘Great Expectation’ Is U.K.’s No. 1 for 2nd Week as Dua Lipa’s ‘Training Season’ Enjoys Viral Surge
summary: The song is Sienna's first U.K. No. 1 single.
contentText:
Sienna Spiro ’s “Great Expectation” is No. 1 on the the U.K.’s Official Singles Chart for a second consecutive week on the chart published Friday (Sept. 18).

Related

Sienna Spiro Becomes Youngest British Female to Top U.K. Singles Chart in 12 Years Thanks to ‘Great Expectation’

Capitol Music Group CEO Tom March on the ‘Incredible’ Sienna Spiro, Breaking Sam Fender in the U.S. & More

On Sept. 11 , the song, taken from her 2026 debut LP Visitor , gave the London-born pop star her first U.K. chart-topper. The achievement made her the youngest British female artist to earn a No. 1 since Becky Hill topped the chart in July 2014 with her Oliver Heldens team-up “Gecko (Overdrive).”

“Great Expectation” dethroned Ella Langley’s Billboard Hot 100 -topping track “Choosin’ Texas,” which has so far scored just one week at the summit. Spiro’s “Die on this Hill” also reenters the top 10, closing the week at No. 10.

Following “Choosin’ Texas” at No. 2 is “Movin’ to the Sun” by Hugel, Imael Angel and Ultra Nate follows at No. 3, while Stella Lefty’s “Boston” stays put at No. 4.

Dua Lipa’s “Training Season” returns to the top five (No. 5) more than two years on from its previous peak at No. 4. The song is currently enjoying a lift on streaming following a social media trend where fans, inspired by Dua, are “manifesting” their future hopes; Dua previously said that she wrote the song prior to meeting her now-husband, Callum Turner, and said the song was “almost like a manifestation.” The song is currently up to No. 5 on Billboard ‘s Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart.

Ashe’s “Stop the Wedding!” enters the top 10 for the first time at No. 9; the song burst into the Hot 100 this past week, landing at No. 96. Adéla’s “Nicole Kidman” rises 35 places week-on-week to No. 15 to earn the Slovak star her second top 20 hit after “Ain’t in LA.”

Recent Chartbreaker Alyssa Grace sees “Bloodstream” earn a new peak at No. 12, while Noah Kahan’s “Orbiter” (No. 22) and “Willing and Able” (No. 35) both hit new highs.
